Ten comments

The following is about this song from the Clarke Tin Whistle book by Bill Ochs: “A recently composed tune by Norman Maclean, piper from Uist in the Outer Hebrides. A friend of his working in London complained about the qulaity of potatoes there, and so this tune was born”

There’s a strong rhythm to this tune which you can emphasise by double-stopping that opening A note (drone an E with it). Alternatively, you could change it from one long A note into a triplet, ABA for example.

There’s some other long notes in the second part where you could do the same thing. So, instead of simply a long E followed by a long A, you’d have EFE ABA.

↳ Posted by Jeremy on June 2nd, 2001.

Scarce O’ Tatties

A fiddler friend of mine, Clay Scott, hauled this one up from the depths of memory along the followling lines--similar to Jeremy’s setting, but for a few notes here and there. We’ve added it to our short list of frequently played tunes at the local session.

Scarce O’ Tatties

I’ve added the version I’m familiar with. We wouldn’t play any Cs in this tune at all. Chord structure and modes aren’t my strong point but A dorian seems more accurate to me. Also, it’s played heavily swung, almost like a 6/8 march, so I’ve added that to the dots too.

↳ Posted by bagpie on November 25th, 2014.

Scarce O’ Tatties, X:9

Just had a look through the list here and realised that none of the settings are the way I play the tune!

Bagpie and Fernando’s are close though..

The setting I originally learned was actually written with no key signature but with the added “F sharps” in the notation. However, to simply things, I’ve added my setting here in “A Dorian” as the above posters have done. I don’t know what’s best?

Apart from the occasional different note depending on my mood, that’s usually the way I still play the tune.
